# Real Property Tax Circuit Breaker Credit - Subsection (e)

## Paragraph (1)(A)(ii) - Qualified Taxpayer Definition (2025+)

For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, a qualified taxpayer must be a resident individual who:
- Has occupied the same residence for six months or more during the tax year
- Has qualifying real property taxes or a real property tax equivalent exceeding specific percentages of federal adjusted gross income

The thresholds range from **3.5% for income of $3,000 or less** up to **6.5% for income over $14,000 but not exceeding $18,000**.

## Paragraph (2) - Amount of Credit

For pre-2025 tax years, the statute specifies: "The credit, computed as described in paragraph two of this subsection, shall not exceed" the tax liability reduced by other permitted credits.

For 2025 and beyond, the structure remains similar but applies to the modified qualified taxpayer definition.

## Key 2025+ Provisions

Starting January 1, 2025, qualifying real property taxes are calculated "less any school tax relief credit allowed under subsection (eee)." Additionally, the definition of "real property tax equivalent" for renters simplifies to "twenty-five percent of the adjusted rent actually paid."

The credit applies only to amounts actually paid by the taxpayer occupying the residence for six months or more.

## Real Property Tax Credit Overview

The real property tax credit may be available to New York State residents who have federal adjusted gross income (FAGI) of $18,000 or less, and pay real property taxes or rent for their residences.

## Credit Amounts

If you and your dependents are under age 65, the credit can be as much as $75. If you, your spouse (if married filing a joint return), or a dependent is age 65 or older, the credit can be as much as $375.

## Eligibility Requirements

To qualify for the real property tax credit for tax year 2025, you must meet all of these conditions: your federal adjusted gross income was $18,000 or less; you occupied the same New York residence for six months or more; you were a New York State resident for all of 2025; you could not be claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's federal income tax return; your residence was not completely exempted from real property taxes; and the current market value of all real property you owned was $85,000 or less.
